archetype: A mono-red critical-mass copy engine wearing an aggro costume. deck-audit matches it to `aggro` from strategic_frame.json and the creature count agrees (27, inside 26-32), but the frame's own reading is right: the 1/1s are not the clock, they are Zada's copy multiplier, Skirk Prospector's mana and Skullclamp's fuel. The kill is a single spell copied N times, not combat.
verdict: This deck functions and it converts: the mana base is at every target, the turn-3 land drop lands 90% of the time, and five checker-passed stacks show what one red mana does once Zada is out — five cards for {R} (001), 8 damage to each opponent off one storm turn (002), 30 trample damage from four 1/1s (003), and a genuinely infinite Storm-Kiln Artist + Haze of Rage loop (005). What limits it is that all of that routes through one unprotected 3/3. The protection axis measures 2, and one of those two — Roaming Throne — wards only itself, so the deck's real insurance on its commander is Swiftfoot Boots and nothing else.

open_questions.question: Cast Daring Discovery targeting only Zada: does her trigger copy it for each other creature, and does each copy's Discover 4 resolve?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Daring Discovery has no entry in `card_roles.json` and is counted by no axis. If the copies each Discover, it is quietly the deck's largest single card-advantage burst and a lean-into; if they do not, it is a five-mana sorcery in a modal-2 deck and the next cut.

open_questions.question: With Roaming Throne naming Goblin, does Zada's copy trigger triggering an additional time produce a second full set of copies?
open_questions.why_it_matters: strategic_frame.json already queues this as a candidate line. It decides whether Roaming Throne is a four-mana doubler of the deck's best effect or a 4/4 body whose Ward {2} the protection axis is miscounting as commander insurance.

open_questions.question: Is Seething Anger + Zada + Storm-Kiln Artist actually infinite, and at what mana?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only pool line that both deepens the thinnest engine component and adds a second verified kill; without a passing stack it stays a candidate and the add rests on the redundancy argument alone.

open_questions.question: Should goldfish_targets.json declare a fourth target for Storm-Kiln Artist + Haze of Rage?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Stack 005 verifies that pair as a true infinite and it is what drives the bracket-4 floor, yet no declared target contains either card — so the deck's best kill has no measured assembly rate and the 15.2% storm figure is being read as if it were the deck's ceiling when it is not.

gaps: No `deck_recon.json` exists for this deck, so nothing here is grounded in what strong Zada lists actually run — there are no per-commander inclusion rates in any artifact in this repo. Every add is argued from this deck's own measurements. Settled by a `deck-recon` pass.

Goldfish models resource development only — no removal, no interaction. Nothing in any artifact measures how often Zada actually survives to the pivot turn, so the protection finding is an argument from card counts and the corpus, not a simulated rate.

`Chaos Warp` has no entry in `card_roles.json`, so the deck's only catch-all answer is invisible to both `interaction` and `interaction-breadth`. The breadth figure of 2 cannot be read as a count of this deck's answers. Same class of miss: `Daring Discovery`, `Spreading Insurrection`, `Fists of Flame` and `Wild Ride` are all unclassified.

strategic_frame.json lists 'No storm/critical-mass theory section' and 'No commander-protection/insurance section' among its gaps. Both sections now exist — `strategy:critical-mass.storm-math` and `strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance` — and are cited throughout this diagnosis, so the frame's gap list is stale on those two entries.

The corpus has no section on a commander whose own ability requires you to target it. That is why Lightning Greaves, the format's default protection, is anti-synergistic here, and no cited rule says so — it is read off the card. Settled by a `research-strategy` pass.

The bench holds one card (Sazacap's Brew) and strategic_frame.json already records why it is not a Zada enabler: it targets a player, so the copy trigger never fires. There is effectively no sideboard to draw on.
